No two consecutive words can share the same first letter. Write a descriptive, fictional, imaginative screenplay of a fish being pulled out of the water by a human and made to stare at the solar eclipse. The fish descends into a lovecraftian monologue about "horrors beyond it's comprehension" and has an existensial crisisassistant
response:
FADE IN:

EXT. BEACH - DAY

The sun beats down on the sandy shore as a human, JEN (30s), wades into the ocean, her eyes scanning the water for signs of life. Suddenly, she spots a fish, FINLEY (a sleek, silver fish), swimming near the surface. She reaches out a hand, and Finley is sucked into her grasp.

JEN
(excitedly)
Oh, look at you! You're so beautiful!

Finley struggles and squirms in Jen's hand, but she holds tight. Jen pulls Finley out of the water and onto the beach, where Finley lies flailing on the sand.

JEN
(curiously)
What's wrong, little guy? You're not used to being out of the water, are you?

Finley looks up at Jen with a mixture of fear and confusion. Jen holds him up to the sky, and Finley's gaze follows the sun as it begins to darken.

JEN
(amused)
Oh, look! A solar eclipse! Isn't it amazing?

Finley's eyes widen in terror as the sun's corona appears, casting an otherworldly glow over the beach. Finley's body begins to convulse, and he speaks in a voice that is both familiar and yet, utterly alien.

FINLEY
(whispering)
The void... it's coming... the void is coming...

JEN
(confused)
What's wrong, Finley? You're scaring me!

FINLEY
(urgently)
You don't understand... the horrors beyond your comprehension... the eldritch abominations that lurk beyond the veil of reality... they're coming for us all...

Finley's monologue grows more frantic, his words tumbling out in a maddening torrent.

FINLEY
(whispering)
The cyclopean cities of R'lyeh... the twisted, non-Euclidean geometry of the abyssal planes... the crawling chaos that defies all rational thought... it's all coming for us...

Jen's expression changes from amusement to alarm as Finley's words paint a picture of a universe that is both beautiful and terrifying.

JEN
(backing away)
Finley, stop! You're scaring me!

FINLEY
(whispering)
You can't escape... the void is always there... waiting to consume us all...

Finley's body begins to contort and twist, his scales glistening with an otherworldly sheen. His eyes roll back in his head, and he speaks in a voice that is no longer his own.

FINLEY
(whispering)
I am but a mere mortal... a fleeting moment in the grand tapestry of existence... and yet... I am aware... I am aware of the horrors that lurk beyond the veil...

Finley's monologue grows more and more incoherent, his words devolving into a cacophony of madness.

FINLEY
(whispering)
I am but a fish... a mere fish... and yet... I am the universe... I am the cosmos... I am the abyss...

Jen stumbles backward, tripping over her own feet as Finley's body begins to dissolve into a pool of writhing, pulsing energy.

JEN
(screaming)
Ahh! Finley! No!

The camera zooms out as Finley's energy dissipates, leaving behind a small, lifeless fish on the sand. Jen stands frozen, her eyes fixed on the spot where Finley once lay.

FADE TO BLACK.

FADE IN:

EXT. BEACH - LATER

Jen stands alone on the beach, the only sound the gentle lapping of the waves against the shore. She looks out at the ocean, a mixture of fear and awe on her face.

JEN
(whispering)
I don't understand... what just happened...

The camera lingers on Jen's face as the sun reappears, casting a warm glow over the beach. But the sense of unease lingers, a reminder that there are horrors beyond human comprehension that lurk just beneath the surface of our reality.

FADE TO BLACK.
